source_binding: This early read-only probe was executed before the new skill module existed. It used the then-loaded src/rules.ts, src/setup.ts, src/game.ts, src/slots.ts, src/spaces.ts and src/settlement.ts. Individual file hashes were not captured at that time, so this record must not be used as an exact-final-source acceptance result.
method: Eight fixed-seed ordinary random playouts, up to 80 actions each. Each accepted action used applyAuthoritativeMove. At each playing boundary, a separate public geometry enumerator counted revealed non-general ground ally/enemy pairs in an unobstructed orthogonal line, distance 2..3 or 2..4, with a one-square pull toward the ally, placementAllowed and final public own-king safety. No new hero ability was executed and no hidden identity/trap was used for candidate selection. Games stopped at the authority's execution stage or 80-action budget; these were not recorded as completed games.
interpretation: The extra fourth square added 8 sampled turns with candidates. This preliminary availability result did not justify widening the chosen range. It says nothing about whether a candidate is strategically valuable, complete rule compatibility or balanced strength.
limitations: Very weak random policy; four early ambush endings had no candidate at either range.
Longer games contribute more sampled positions; the fractions are not per-game or per-player success rates.
No actual new-hero execution or 4-square variant implementation.
No exact source hash binding; do not include in release test pass totals.
This observation is retained for the design decision history, not as a claim of global balance.
